adviceSentences.normal: Your physiological and psychological parameters are perfectly aligned with spaceflight targets.
adviceSentences.watch: A slight metabolic or fatigue drift is observed. Maintain your rest and hydration routines.
adviceSentences.action: Multiple indicators signal an elevated physiological strain. Adjust your rest and exercise schedule.
adviceSentences.contact_flight_surgeon: A critical result was detected. Priority medical contact with Earth is required.

home.noAlerts: No active alerts. All vital systems stable.

body.selectZone: Click on any body area to display comprehensive analytical details

panel.projectionNote: Simple linear projection, not a clinical prediction.

heart.whatIsIt: Monitors resting blood pressure regulation and resting heart rate stability.
heart.spaceEffect: In microgravity, body fluids shift toward the head, reducing plasma volume and elevating orthostatic intolerance risk upon return.
whatToDo: Maintain 2 hours of daily cardiovascular and resistive training.
Adhere to the prescribed hydration and electrolyte intake.
Transition postures gradually to avoid lightheadedness.

bone.whatIsIt: Assesses bone mineral density and muscular mass preservation in load-bearing regions (spine, femoral neck, hip).
bone.spaceEffect: Lack of mechanical loading accelerates bone resorption over formation, causing 0.5% to 1% monthly bone loss if unprotected.
whatToDo: Never skip resistance training sessions on the ARED device.
Take daily vitamin D3 supplements and meet dietary calcium targets.
Record any joint or bone discomfort promptly.

belly.whatIsIt: Tracks capillary blood glucose stability and metabolic energy balance.
belly.spaceEffect: Confinement and neuroendocrine stress can induce transient insulin resistance and alter gut microbiome absorption.
whatToDo: Choose meals with moderate glycemic indices.
Maintain consistent hydration throughout waking hours.
Perform a verification check 2 hours post-meal if needed.

skin.whatIsIt: Monitors core body temperature and febrile or inflammatory responses.
skin.spaceEffect: Absence of natural convection in microgravity impedes sweat evaporation, posing a risk of 'space fever' during and after workouts.
whatToDo: Ensure personal cabin and exercise ventilation fans remain active.
Towel off thoroughly following physical exertion.
Report any temperature ≥ 38 °C immediately to the flight surgeon.

radiation.whatIsIt: Measures cumulative ionizing radiation dose from galactic cosmic rays and solar particle events.
radiation.spaceEffect: Beyond Earth's protective magnetosphere, deep-space radiation penetrates vehicle shielding and increases lifetime health risks.
whatToDo: Check and log the active dosimeter reading daily.
In the event of a solar particle event (SPE) alert, retreat immediately to the storm shelter.
Verify that the dosimeter sensor indicates normal operating range.

mental.title: Psychological Well-Being & Sleep
mental.subtitle: Autonomous assessment of emotional balance, psychological vitality, and sleep recovery.
mental.doctorAlertNotice: ⚠️ Critical result: a priority medical alert has been automatically added to the confidential flight surgeon report.
questions: I have felt cheerful and in good spirits.
I have felt calm and relaxed.
I have felt active and vigorous.
I woke up feeling fresh and rested.
My daily life has been filled with things that interest me.

choices.label: More than half of the time
Less than half of the time

normal.title: Optimal Psychological Well-Being
normal.phrase: Your level of vitality, calmness, and daily engagement is excellent and strongly supports long-duration mission resilience.
actions: Maintain your positive daily relaxation and physical training habits.
Keep up regular informal conversations and shared meals with crewmates.
Continue scheduled video contacts with loved ones on Earth.

watch.title: Watch: Moderate dip in vitality
watch.phrase: A mild decrease in energy or emotional calm has been reported over recent days.
actions: Protect your 8-hour sleep block in your crew quarters.
Share how you are feeling with a trusted crewmate.
Retake this assessment in 3 to 4 days.

action.title: Action Advised: Significant strain or low mood
action.phrase: Your responses suggest noticeable mental strain or a dip in morale and daily motivation.
actions: Carve out quiet personal time for reading or calming music.
Discuss potential workload adjustments with the mission commander.
Practice guided heart-rate coherence and relaxation breathing sessions.

contact_flight_surgeon.title: Alert: Flight Surgeon Contact Required
contact_flight_surgeon.phrase: Your level of exhaustion or emotional distress requires prompt, confidential support from the ground medical team.
actions: Schedule a confidential call with the flight surgeon or mission psychologist.
Take an immediate rest period in your sleep station.
Report any changes in sleep continuity or appetite to the medical officer.

influences.text: A sleep duration over 7 hours with minimal awakenings directly stabilizes next-day mood (+12%).

influences.title: Consistent exercise
influences.text: The mandatory 2-hour daily workout on ARED and treadmill boosts endorphins and counters isolation stress.

influences.title: Confinement and monotony
influences.text: Sensory deprivation in enclosed habitats increases mental fatigue: protect crew rituals and variety.

missions.environmentReminderTitle: Operational Guidance for Your Mission Environment

spacecraft.title: Deep Space Transit Protocol
spacecraft.text: Mandatory 2 hours of daily cardiovascular and resistive training to preserve orthostatic tolerance and mitigate muscular atrophy.

station.title: Orbital Microgravity Protocol
station.text: Daily workout sessions on ARED resistance device and T2 treadmill are essential to counter progressive bone demineralization.

lunar_base.title: Lunar Surface Protocol (1/6 g)
lunar_base.text: Monitor partial mechanical loading, record daily surface dosimeter reading, and follow regolith dust decontamination procedures.

mars_rover.title: Martian Exploration Protocol (1/3 g)
mars_rover.text: Earth communications delay of 15 to 20 minutes: strict daily self-assessment of vitals, active dosimeter monitoring, and complete medical autonomy.

firstContact.name: First Contact
firstContact.desc: At least one self-assessment successfully logged on board.

martianEndurance.name: Martian Endurance
martianEndurance.desc: 60-day consecutive streak of complete telemetry protocol.

cognitive.reactionProtocol1: Get comfortable and keep a finger ready to tap the screen.
cognitive.reactionProtocol2: Tap the response area only when it changes color.
cognitive.reactionProtocol3: After 2 practice trials, 8 trials are timed; wait for the signal and avoid anticipating it.
cognitive.orientationProtocol1: Look at the arrow shown in the center of the dial.
cognitive.orientationProtocol2: Choose which of the eight directions the arrow points toward.
cognitive.orientationProtocol3: After one practice trial, 8 trials are recorded; take your time and answer without outside help.
cognitive.reactionInstructions: Two practice trials come before the 8 measured trials. Tap the area as soon as it appears.
cognitive.orientationInstructions: Identify the direction indicated by the arrow. Accuracy and mean response time are recorded.
cognitive.disclaimer: Informal exercise, not validated for diagnosis. Results also depend on the display, input method, vision, and fatigue.
cognitive.nonDiagnostic: Recorded as a personal tracking indicator only, without interpretation or medical thresholds.
